questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

The women in the team has showcased exceptional teamwork and dedication.
questions.solution_en:
The correct option that can substitute the underlined segment is 'have demonstrated exceptional'. The error in the original sentence is related to subject-verb agreement. The singular 'has' in the sentence does not match with the plural subject 'women'. "Women" is a plural noun, so it should be followed by the plural verb "have," not the singular "has."

Option (d) correctly substitutes "has" with "have" to match the plural subject "women."

Options (a) and (b) are incorrect because they do not address the subject-verb agreement error in the original sentence. Both 'has' and 'is' are singular and do not match with the plural subject 'women'. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: The women in the team have demonstrated exceptional teamwork and dedication.

NOTE:

Subject-verb agreement means that a subject and its verb must be both singular or plural:

A singular subject takes a singular verb.

A plural subject takes a plural verb.

For example, in the sentence 'John lives in France', the subject John (singular 'he') 'agrees with' the third person singular form of the verb to live - lives.

questions.q_en: Describe how you will say 'Do you know the exact location?' in passive voice.
options_en: Is the exact location known of you?
Does the exact location known by you?
Is the exact location known to you?
Is the exact location known with you?
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The question in Active voice is an interrogative sentence. The answer to this question will be either "yes" or "no".

These types of sentences usually begin with a helping verb like: Do, does.

The format of such a sentence in Active voice is: Do/Does + Subject + V1 + Object?

Therefore, in Passive voice, the format will be: Am/Is/Are + Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case)?

For example:

Does he need therapy? (Active)

Is therapy needed by him? (Passive)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The match will be won by the team. A new record will be set by them.

Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.solution_en:
Imperative Sentences are used to demonstrate Request, Order, Command, etc.

The reporting verbs like "said", "say", etc. in direct speech are changed into "begged", "beg", etc.

Therefore, the correct answer is: "The teacher said to read the instructions carefully."

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

With cracked plaster and peeling paint, I considered what I could say. Water damage would've been the easy answer, but I opted for the truth: "My phone rang." As expected, these words settled somewhere beyond her reach, so she gave my comment its only sensible response: "Maybe you should turn down the ringer." "Come here, let me explain why I hate phones, and why my father is to blame. He was a troubled man," I said, because that's how it had been said to me. She listened with attentive eyes, but I knew she'd be confused by what I said next: "And he'd play Nulla in Mundo Pax Sincera. Over and over." She lowered her head in search of a link and looked up when she found one. "Is that solitaire?" This time I allowed a smile. "Sometimes he'd conduct an invisible orchestra, waving arms in an erratic fashion, and sometimes he'd sit and listen. But Nulla in Mundo Pax Sincera, that one commanded a different reaction. From the start, he stood at full attention, motionless until the end. It went like this for a long time, then he left."

"I soon became his replacement. I'd sit in the study and listen to his music. One evening mother said he wanted to talk to me. I asked if I was going to see him and she said that he'd call. I asked if I could use the phone in his study and she said I could." At this point my companion, attentive as ever, offered her second assumption of the evening, and though more likely than the first, it was just as wrong: "And he never called and that's why you hate phones." No, that's not why. "When mother told me he was on the line, I rushed to the study and dropped the needle on Nulla in Mundo Pax Sincera, then picked up the phone. He didn't say hello or ask how I was, he only said that there's no peace in the world. He'd looked, it wasn't there, not for him." With her final assumption, she came closer to the truth: "So phones remind you of your father, and that's why you hate them."

"That's part of it," I said, "but there's more. He said he could hear Vivaldi in the background and told me to keep listening, that aria was on to something. Then he said goodbye to me and mother and everyone else. Forever. He found his peace." The music prevented a silence that would've felt more comfortable, then it finally stopped and I let the silence prevail. And there we sat, speaking without speaking, until the silence was shattered by a ring. I stood and walked to the phone, picked it up, not just the receiver, but all of it, and paused to admire the artistry.

What did the speaker do after learning that the father was on the line?
options_en: She/he went inside to dress up.
The speaker played the father's favourite piece of music.
She/he went to the room to stop the music so that she/he could listen to the father.
She/he went outside to avoid calls.
questions.solution_en: The second paragraph states that "When mother told me he was on the line, I rushed to the study and dropped the needle on Nulla in Mundo Pax Sincera, then picked up the phone." So, option (c) is the correct choice.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The boss said that he would be attending a client meeting the following Monday.
options_en: The boss said, "I would being attending a client meeting next Monday."
The boss said, "I will be attending a client meeting the following Monday."
The boss said, "I will be attending a client meeting next Monday."
The boss said, "I will have been attending a client meeting next Monday."
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is (c) The boss said, "I will be visiting a client meeting next Monday."

Key points:

• The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Conditional Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Future Continuous Tense.

• Conditional Continuous (Subject + would/should + be +V1 +ing + Object) will be converted into Future Continuous (Subject + will/shall + be + V1 + ing + Object).

• For example:

o He said that he would be using the book the following Friday. (Indirect Speech)

o He said, "I will be using the book next Friday" (Direct Speech)

• The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:
Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
said that hesaid...I
would be visiting...the followingwill be visiting...next

• Therefore, the correct answer is: The boss said, "I will be visiting a client meeting next Monday."
